text:
alex: quick proposal — introduce an "adaptive deprecation broadcaster" to signal deprecations to clients and orchestrate shim rollouts. idea is a short-lived header + telemetry events so clients can opt in to automated shims, and we can animate gradual rollforward/rollback waves. thoughts?

jen: ooo interesting. want a one-way signal or a two-way handshake?

kavi: probably both. server emits header + event, client ACKs once it installed/accepted shim. fallback if no ACK after N requests. keep it simple initially. :+1:

alex: yeah plan A: emit `X-RW-Dep-Signal: v3;expires=1718600000;gradewave=1` on infra edge. clients that understand it can respond with `X-RW-Dep-Ack: v3` on first request. if ack absent after 30s, route to backward-compatible shim.

ryan: what's the shim surface? is it a proxy-side transform or server-side translator? both have tradeoffs. proxy-side is faster to iterate, server-side has better telemetry.

jen: prefer proxy-side for initial waves (safer, no model change). we already have sidecar infra for envelopes. reuse that for shim instance.

alex: agreed — sidecar shim for wave 0/1, then move to compiled server shim for performance if stable. we need a clear kill-switch. maybe a per-tenant `dep.disable` flag and a global emergency boolean in control plane.

kavi: telemetry we should emit: `dep.signal.sent`, `dep.ack.received`, `dep.shim.fallback`, `dep.rollback.triggered`. attach tenant id + sample of request shape hash. also track latency delta in shim.

ryan: rollout strategy: 1) internal canary, 2) opt-in beta tenants, 3) progressive percent-based wave, 4) full default. each wave should auto-failover on a spike in `dep.shim.fallback` or error rate.

jen: test matrix: - schema diffs (missing fields) - streaming frame differences - auth header transforms - size/regression perf. we should add unit-level golden prompts for quality checks.

alex: operational notes: add a `deprecation-broadcaster` job that annotates edge responses. broadcaster exposes dry-run mode (header logged but not enforced), active mode (header + routing), and emergency-off. config via console with per-tenant overrides.

ryan: one more: migration safety — keep both code paths compiled with feature gate; warmup caches for new path before switching route. no cold-start during wave.

kavi: security/consent question — do we require explicit tenant opt-in for automatic shim install? some enterprise customers will want manual opt-in. we should make automatic opt-in default for non-enterprise and opt-in for enterprise via account setting.

alex: good call. make default auto-opt-in, but allow accounts to flip `auto_deprecate_opt_in=false`. record consent event.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: note — adding broadcaster will add 1x to edge latency in dry-run mode (measured), and sidecar shims add variable latency depending on transform complexity.

jen: next steps: 1) RFC doc with example headers and event schemas, 2) strawman control-plane UI, 3) small PoC sidecar implementation for envelope shim. i'll draft the RFC and ping infra for experiments.

alex: thanks — i'll sketch header/event schema and gating semantics and post as follow-up. tagging @ryan for rollout ops and @kavi for telemetry schema. :rocket:
